svg.title: A gap in stimulation can have neural structure
svg.desc: A: delay versus trace conditioning timelines; in delay conditioning the predictive stimulus (CS) and predicted event (US) overlap, in trace conditioning a stimulus-free gap separates them; a table reports that hippocampal-pallium lesions in goldfish spared delay conditioning and impaired trace conditioning. B: in a rat object-delay-odor task, four schematic CA1 activity profiles peak at successive times during the roughly 10 s delay. C: three illustrative cells compared across an original (about 10 s) and a lengthened (about 20 s) delay on the same 0-20 s scale: timing retained, timing rescaled, and a new time field.

g.text: CS: predictive stimulus; US: predicted event
Rat object-delay-odor task; dorsal CA1 recordings
The earlier object guides the response to the later odor.
Schematic examples from different trial blocks.
